topics.title: Native CSS Nesting & Scoped Organization
topics.summary: Use modern nesting to keep component rules together without recreating deep preprocessor selector chains.

concepts.name: Native nesting
concepts.explanation: Nested selectors can be written inside a parent rule. The & nesting selector explicitly references the parent selector in states and variants.

concepts.name: Keep depth shallow
concepts.explanation: Nesting is organizational syntax, not a reason to create tightly coupled DOM selectors. Deep nesting makes components hard to move and override.

concepts.name: Scope strategy
concepts.explanation: Modern CSS increasingly supports local scoping tools; even without them, component classes and cascade layers should define intentional boundaries.

topics.challenge: Write a component rule using native nesting for a child, a state, and a variant.
topics.hint: Use & where the nested selector modifies or extends the parent selector.

topics.title: Modern Color Spaces & Color Functions
topics.summary: Work with alpha-aware modern syntax, color-mix(), relative color, perceptual spaces, and theme tokens while preserving contrast.

concepts.name: Perceptual spaces
concepts.explanation: oklab() and oklch() are designed around perceptual properties, making lightness and color adjustments more predictable than raw RGB changes.

concepts.name: Color mixing
concepts.explanation: color-mix() creates derived colors at computed-value time and works well with custom properties for borders, hover states, and overlays.

concepts.name: Contrast responsibility
concepts.explanation: A mathematically smooth palette can still be unreadable. Verify text/background contrast and state differences with accessibility tooling.

topics.challenge: Define an OKLCH accent token and derive at least one related color with color-mix().
topics.hint: Keep the source color as a custom property so derived states stay related to the same design token.

topics.title: Advanced Grid, Intrinsic Constraints & Overflow
topics.summary: Solve dense application layouts by combining grid track sizing, minimum-size behavior, overflow rules, and content constraints.

concepts.name: Automatic minimums
concepts.explanation: Grid and flex items can refuse to shrink because their automatic minimum size is content-based. min-width: 0 or minmax(0, 1fr) often fixes unexpected overflow.

concepts.name: Track strategy
concepts.explanation: Use minmax(), fit-content(), subgrid, and auto-fit/auto-fill intentionally rather than stacking breakpoints to fight content.

concepts.name: Overflow is a signal
concepts.explanation: Clipping or scrolling may be correct, but unexplained overflow often reveals an incorrect minimum size, unbreakable content, or overly rigid track.

topics.challenge: Create a sidebar/main layout that resists content overflow using fit-content and minmax(0, 1fr).
topics.hint: When the flexible track still overflows, inspect the grid item minimum size and long unbreakable content.

topics.title: Accessible Themes, Motion & Forced-Color Resilience
topics.summary: Design themes and interaction states that remain understandable across dark mode, reduced motion, high contrast/forced colors, and keyboard input.

concepts.name: Color-scheme
concepts.explanation: color-scheme can inform the browser which light/dark schemes native controls and default surfaces support.

concepts.name: Forced colors
concepts.explanation: forced-colors environments may replace author colors. Avoid communicating state only through subtle color and test system high-contrast modes.

concepts.name: Motion and focus
concepts.explanation: Respect reduced-motion preference and keep clear focus-visible indicators. Accessibility variants should be part of the design system, not emergency patches.

topics.challenge: Add focus-visible styling plus reduced-motion and forced-colors adaptations.
topics.hint: Test meaning with author colors removed; borders, text, and native control states should still communicate structure.

topics.title: Professional CSS Systems & Debugging Capstone
topics.summary: Diagnose cascade, layout, overflow, stacking, responsiveness, and rendering problems systematically while keeping a scalable architecture.

concepts.name: Debug the computed result
concepts.explanation: Use developer tools to inspect which declaration won, which values were inherited, and which rules are crossed out before adding overrides.

concepts.name: Debug layout from the container outward
concepts.explanation: Check the formatting context, available size, minimums, overflow, and track/flex rules before changing child margins at random.

concepts.name: Architecture and measurement
concepts.explanation: Use layers, tokens, component boundaries, responsive containers, and performance measurements as parts of one system. Avoid “fixes” that only work at the current viewport.

topics.challenge: Build a compact CSS system using a layer order, tokens, a responsive grid, and an accessible focus utility.
topics.hint: Treat the challenge as architecture: the rules should still make sense when there are twenty components, not only one demo card.
